name: Virtue USD
oneLiner: VUSD is Virtue Money's CDP dollar on IOTA, minted by borrowing against overcollateralized IOTA and stIOTA positions with liquidation defending the peg.
collateral: Overcollateralized IOTA, stIOTA, vIOTA, and iBTC positions backing VUSD debt inside the Virtue Money protocol
pegMechanism: CDP-style mint: users borrow VUSD against IOTA or stIOTA collateral and repay debt to unlock collateral, with liquidation and redemption mechanics supporting the U.S. dollar peg

oracleRisk.summary: Virtue's four debt-bearing IOTA Move vaults use one configured oracle rule per collateral. IOTA and iBTC depend on single Pyth feeds with the Pyth State's 60-second stale-price threshold; stIOTA and vIOTA derive their values from their native staking pools and inherit the same single IOTA/USD Pyth path.

branchApplicability.rationale: At IOTA checkpoint 166884205, the VUSD Treasury authorized exactly one current mint module, VirtueCDP. A type-wide query of that module returned exactly four live shared Vault objects, all with nonzero debt supply: IOTA, stIOTA, vIOTA, and iBTC. The oracle package likewise exposed exactly four matching PriceAggregater objects, so each debt-bearing branch is reviewed below.

branches.label: IOTA vault
branches.summary: The IOTA vault uses a one-of-one PriceAggregater whose only accepted rule reads the Pyth IOTA/USD feed.

feeds.path: Pyth IOTA/USD c7b72e5d860034288c9335d4d325da4272fe50c92ab72249d58f6cbba30e4c44 -> sole PythRule weight 1 of threshold 1 -> Virtue IOTA PriceResult

branches.fallbackBehavior: The aggregator has one rule and a threshold of one. Its PythRule calls Pyth get_price, which applies the Pyth State's 60-second stale-price threshold; an unsupported identifier, stale or invalid Pyth result, or missing rule aborts the transaction. No fallback or last-good cache is configured.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-reviewed 2026-07-31. At IOTA checkpoint 172877784 (timestamp 2026-07-30 23:13:50 UTC), the immutable VUSD package 0xd3b63e603a78786facf65ff22e79701f3e824881a12fa3268d62a75530fe904f exposes mint/burn, supply-limit, beneficiary, and module-version administration, but no freeze, blacklist, pause, denylist, or holder-transfer hook in its admin, limited_supply, or vusd module function sets; ordinary Move coin transfers therefore have no issuer-selected holder block surface. The inherited stIOTA/vIOTA collateral pools are separate collateral dependencies, not VUSD holder registries. The IOTA EVM address 0x10740259a1860af3327dd0642ee35d6e8e7143ff was re-read at block 12603860 (name Virtue USD, symbol VUSD, decimals 6); the published ERC20Coin implementation exposes vanilla transfer/approve/allowance/transferFrom and delegates account movement to ISC, with no freeze, blacklist, pause, or seize function. The ISC bridge can control cross-chain representation/issuance, but that is route-level mint/burn authority, not selective censorship of existing VUSD holders.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 access review
blacklistabilityReview.upstreamSuppressionRationale: Suppresses a resolver same-symbol/text false positive, confirmed 2026-07-31: the inferred upstream signal comes from "CDP" in the peg-mechanism text and "Money" in "Virtue Money" matching the unrelated tracked coins cdp-enosys (CDP) and money-defi-money (MONEY). VUSD's actual collateral is IOTA, stIOTA, vIOTA, and iBTC, none of which is a freezable upstream stablecoin; that collateral remains a backing dependency, and ISC route-level mint/burn authority remains a bridge-route risk, neither being VUSD holder blacklistability.

reserveReview.rationale: Fresh capture 2026-07-31 at IOTA checkpoint 172877784 (timestamp 2026-07-30 23:13:50 UTC) reads all four live shared Virtue vaults and the shared Stability Pool. Vault balances were 669,463.125762316 IOTA, 25,940,400.259379815 stIOTA, 57,017.073454695 vIOTA, and 0.0149549784 iBTC; VUSD debt supplies were 14,725.933422, 538,673.551046, 1,138.959800, and 732.517975 respectively. Current Swirl and TokenLabs NativePool objects plus cert::Metadata objects give exchange rates 1.1466223329 IOTA/stIOTA and 1.0500262411 IOTA/vIOTA. Pyth Hermes prices published 2026-07-30 23:16:58 UTC were $0.03252683 IOTA/USD and $64,876.40913043 BTC/USD. The resulting collateral values are approximately $21,775.51, $967,472.90, $1,947.36, and $970.23, normalized to 2.19%, 97.51%, 0.20%, and 0.10% (100.00% total). The shared Stability Pool read separately showed 176,231.229596 VUSD across 190 positions. The composition is fully identified at the capture point; no independent reserve attestation or legal custody assurance is published.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Current on-chain branch balances and NativePool exchange rates, valued with the exact Pyth feeds consumed by Virtue's deployed oracle rules and cross-checked against Virtue's CDP collateral documentation
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: No unidentified direct collateral or tracked-stablecoin dependency remains at the 2026-07-31 checkpoint capture; all four slices are external cryptoasset identities rather than Pharos-tracked stablecoins. Independent reserve assurance, legal segregation, and guaranteed liquidation liquidity are not disclosed and are recorded in custodyProfile rather than as an unidentified composition slice.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: The fresh capture shows collateral in four shared protocol vault objects and VUSD in one shared Stability Pool (190 positions), so on-chain custody is omnibus at the protocol/branch level rather than an identified bank or segregated account. The package is immutable but an AdminCap gates supply limits and module versions, and liquidations run through a configured executor. No independent reserve attestation, legal segregation statement, bankruptcy-remoteness opinion, rehypothecation policy, or other assurance report covering the current collateral was found in the reviewed issuer documentation, audit, or on-chain sources; latest assurance scope is therefore unavailable.

controls.evidence: At IOTA Rebased (confirmed via iota_getObject): AdminCap object 0x38a7b38d0f03338397d1c57f2cc2e3d7c5e3f6fe6887626aacc4cb4e8072c3f5 is owned by AddressOwner 0xf67d0193e9cd65c3c8232dbfe0694eb9e14397326bdc362a4fe9d590984f5a12 (version 591278735). The admin module exposes no public entry functions but AdminCap gates vusd::set_supply_limit, add_version, remove_module, remove_version, and set_beneficiary. Whether this address is a single EOA or a multisig could not be determined on-chain.

review.evidence: IOTA Rebased GraphQL confirmed AdminCap (type 0xd3b63e...::admin::AdminCap) is held by address 0xf67d0193e9cd65c3c8232dbfe0694eb9e14397326bdc362a4fe9d590984f5a12 (AddressOwner). iota_getNormalizedMoveModulesByPackage revealed vusd module exposing set_supply_limit, add_version, remove_module, remove_version, set_beneficiary — all AdminCap-gated. Package owner type = Immutable (cannot be re-published). The AdminCap holder address owns no other enumerable objects, so it may be a multisig or single-keypair; cannot confirm threshold/type from chain state alone. Promotion judgment: the AdminCap holder address is confirmed on-chain; on Move-VM chains an address holder is EOA-equivalent (single-key vs k-of-n keypair custody is indistinguishable from chain state, matching the EVM EOA custody rule and the standard applied to BUCK and suiUSDe on Sui). All mint-capable surfaces (immutable branch contracts; parameter-only AdminCap) are confirmed. Economic cap reviewed 2026-07-20: the CDP branch cap is not a firm bound, because vusd::set_supply_limit is gated only by the AdminCap held at a single Move address with no timelock and no independent co-signer evidenced on chain. Under the v9 authoring contract a self-controlled, no-timelock raiseable cap is economically unbounded, so economicCapSemantics is recorded as unbounded rather than left encoding-derived. This supersedes the contract-encoding cap only; directMintAbility is unchanged.
